about: ONE FIXTURE FOR BOTH SHELLS (#1188, A2/A8): what a shell does when Rust sends a ScheduleNotifications. `wanted` is the set's `all` (id, fire_at_ms, immediate); `live` its `live_ids`; `pending` the ids the OS holds scheduled; `showing` the ids the OS is showing. The plan lists are sorted for removePending and removeShowing, and in the set's order for schedule and post. THE RULE: pending ones leave when not scheduled again; a showing one leaves only when its id is in neither `wanted` nor `live`, so time passing never removes a delivered reminder and resolving the item does. Read by NotifyPlanTest (Android) and NotificationPlanTests (iOS).

cases.name: a future one is scheduled and nothing else happens
an id no longer wanted leaves pending and showing
a delivered reminder whose time has passed stays while the item is live
a delivered reminder whose item was resolved goes
a wanted one already past is not scheduled and a banner for it stays
an immediate receipt is posted once
an immediate receipt already showing is not posted again
the last of a repeated id wins
an empty set cancels everything pending and everything showing that is not live
a delivered banner past the live bound is not named and goes, though its item is open
